newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels bourse to suffer more from healthy purge.
newsitem.headline: Brussels bourse to suffer more from healthy purge.

text.p: The Brussels bourse is set for further consolidation with no support for the Bel-20 in sight until the share index sheds another 50-odd points, dealers said after Wednesday's session of renewed weakness.

The index was in the middle of the day's range at the end of another bourse session marked by profit-taking after recent strong gains, in part inspired by further losses on Wall Street and rising bond yields.
The Bel-20, which added 150 points last week in a continuous stream of record-breaking sessions, gave up 12.48 points to end at 2,347.55 after having lost 27.37 points on Tuesday.
The bourse had bounced back towards the end of the morning, but losses deepened again late in the day as Wall Street suffered from profit-taking in two hi-tech stocks.
Dealers said the ongoing correction was healthy.

"The balloon is being deflated," an analyst said, forecasting there was not much more selling potential. "We will be entering a quieter period." The bourse as a rule calms down in the holiday months of July and August after bouts of action during the annual dividend payout period.
He said the market had already reached his 1997 target of 2,300 points on the Bel-20. "Now things will slow down."

Fundamentally, the market should remain well-supported. "If first-half corporate profits are good and the dollar and interest rates remain steady, there will not be much movement on shares in the near term," he added.
Analysts foresee no change in key interest rates until the second quarter of 1998. Company profits are expected to have benefitted from the gradual pick-up in economies in Europe.

Others were also positive about the current correction, saying the recent rise to a record high of 2,410 went too quickly. The index could now slip another 50, possibly 100, points before the correction was completed.
Some analysts warned evidence of strength in U.S. economic data and forecasts of more to come could spark fresh profit- taking. They advised short-term players to use upticks to sell.
Wednesday's main losers among Bel-20 shares included non-ferrous mining company Union Miniere, with some of the selling linked to Friday's options expiries.
Chemicals, films and drugs UCB continued to correct down from recent sharp gains; Solvay slipped, having bounced off a recent high.

Among retailers Delhaize was being unloaded for GIB, upgraded by Generale Bank, and Colruyt. Among banks Kredietbank was hit by fading merger talk and a downgrade from brokers Merrill Lynch. Bank BBL benefitted, ending higher.
